gen-gf-phudu-gf-inria-sans: Phudu's open-ended curves look like ballpoint ink, bold but pressure-free. Inria Sans holds the text in tubular strokes, so the heading does the shouting and the body does the explaining.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-istok-web: Thin-looking yet loud, Phudu draws every letter as one plain line with no thinner parts at all. Istok Web stays low and rounded beneath it.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-jost: Distinctive from the first glance, Phudu is bold with open curve endings. Jost follows in the sans-serif text with broad terminal gaps and a unit-width stroke, so the heading gets noticed and the lines below stay easy to follow.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-jura: Jura handles the text with strokes as constant as bent wire. Phudu takes the heading, bold and distinctive, so make it noticeably bigger than Jura's lines to get the full effect.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-kanchenjunga: Bold, distinctive Phudu opens every curve and draws with a pressure-free ballpoint line. And Kanchenjunga, a plain sans with the steady line of a drafting pen, holds the text without clogging at low resolution.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-kantumruy-pro: Loud, pen-simple lettering with open curve endings. Kantumruy Pro, a plain sans with an e that opens clearly to the right, gives Phudu's heading an approachable, hairline-free partner underneath.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-kodchasan: Kodchasan sets its terminals hanging open and skips any calligraphic thinning, which makes the plain sans body quiet. Give its text a generous size and let Phudu's heading stay bold.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-koho: Phudu looks like spaghetti spelled out in letters. KoHo, a plain sans with wide c apertures, sits low and tidy underneath, so the heading gets the swagger and the text stays out of its way.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-kosugi: Bold, distinctive Phudu, drawn like a ballpoint line with open curve endings. Kosugi, a plain sans with an open-jawed c and a wire-bent look, would carry a longer passage with a clean, professional feel.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-kosugi-maru: Phudu draws bold letters with generous openings on every curve and a pressure-free line. And Kosugi Maru adds sans text like neon tubing, far-apart stroke ends glowing in one steady thickness.
